units.zh: 阿柴虜吐谷渾，遼東鮮卑也。
units.en: The Tuyuhun—whom the northwestern tribes called the "A-Chai" barbarians—were Xianbei from Liaodong.
units.literal: The Tuyuhun, whom the northwestern tribes called the A-Chai barbarians, were Xianbei from Liaodong.

units.zh: 父弈洛韓，有二子，長曰吐谷渾，少曰若洛廆。
units.en: Their father Yiluohan had two sons—the elder named Tuyuhun, the younger Ruoluohe.
units.literal: Their father Yiluohan had two sons: the elder was called Tuyuhun, the younger Ruoluohe.

units.zh: 若洛廆別為慕容氏。
units.en: Ruoluohe's descendants formed the Murong clan as a separate line.
units.literal: Ruoluohe's line became the Murong clan separately.

units.zh: 渾庶長，廆正嫡。
units.en: Hun was the elder son of a concubine, while Hui was the legitimate heir.
units.literal: Hun was the elder son by a concubine; Hui was the legitimate heir.

units.zh: 父在時，分七百戶與渾，[2]渾與廆二部俱牧馬，馬鬭相傷，廆怒，遣信謂渾曰：「先公處分，與兄異部，牧馬何不相遠，而致鬭爭相傷？」
units.en: While their father was still alive he allotted seven hundred households to Hun. [2] The two divisions of Hun and Hui pastured their horses together; when the herds fought and injured one another, Hui grew angry and sent a messenger to Hun, saying, "Our late father placed you and me in separate divisions—why not pasture farther apart, instead of letting the horses fight and wound each other?"
units.literal: While their father was alive he allotted seven hundred households to Hun. [2] Hun and Hui's two divisions both pastured horses together; the horses fought and injured one another. Hui grew angry and sent a messenger to say to Hun: "Our late father's arrangement placed you and me in separate divisions—why do we not pasture our horses farther apart, yet instead bring fighting and injury?"

units.zh: 渾曰：「馬是畜生，食草飲水，春氣發動，所以致鬭。
units.en: Hun replied, "Horses are animals—they graze and drink; when spring stirs them, they fight. That is all.
units.literal: Hun said: "Horses are beasts—they eat grass and drink water; when spring qi stirs, that is why they fight.

units.zh: 鬭在於馬，而怒及人邪。
units.en: The quarrel is between the horses—why turn your anger on me?
units.literal: The fighting is among the horses—why take anger at a person?

units.zh: 乖別甚易，今當去汝萬里。」
units.en: Parting is easy enough—I shall now put ten thousand li between us."
units.literal: Separation is very easy; now I shall leave you ten thousand li away."

units.zh: 於是擁馬西行，日移一頓，頓八十里。
units.en: With that he drove his herds westward, advancing one day's march at a time—eighty li per march.
units.literal: Thereupon he drove his horses westward, moving one stage each day, each stage eighty li.

units.zh: 經數頓，廆悔悟，深自咎責，遣舊父老及長史乙那樓追渾令還。
units.en: After several days' march Hui repented and reproached himself deeply; he sent the old clan elders and Chief Clerk Yi Nalou to overtake Hun and bring him back.
units.literal: After several stages Hui came to regret it, blamed himself deeply, and sent the elders of former days and Chief Clerk Yi Nalou to pursue Hun and bring him back.

units.zh: [3]渾曰：「我乃祖以來，樹德遼右，又卜筮之言，先公有二子，福胙並流子孫。
units.en: [3] Hun said, "Since my grandfather's day our house has built its virtue east of the Liao, and divination had declared that our late father had two sons and that blessing and sacrificial fortune would flow to both lines of descendants.
units.literal: [3] Hun said: "From my grandfather's time we have planted virtue east of the Liao; moreover divination said our late father had two sons and that blessings and sacrificial portions would both flow to their descendants.

units.zh: 我是卑庶，理無並大，今以馬致別，殆天所啟。
units.en: I am of low birth and cannot by right stand equal with the heir; that horses should now force our parting is perhaps Heaven's own prompting.
units.literal: I am lowborn and of inferior status; by principle I cannot stand equal with the great; now horses have brought about separation—perhaps Heaven is opening the way.

units.zh: 諸君試擁馬令東，馬若還東，我當相隨去。」
units.en: Try, all of you, driving the horses east—if they turn back eastward, I shall return with you."
units.literal: You gentlemen, try driving the horses east; if the horses return east, I shall go back with you."

units.zh: 樓喜拜曰：「處可寒。」
units.en: Lou bowed gladly and said, "Chukhan!"
units.literal: Lou bowed with joy and said: "Chukhan."

units.zh: 虜言「處可寒」，宋言爾官家也。
units.en: In their tongue "chukhan" means, in the language of Song, "your lordship."
units.literal: In barbarian speech "chukhan" means, in Song language, "your lordship."

units.zh: 即使所從二千騎共遮馬令回，不盈三百步，欻然悲鳴突走，聲若頹山。
units.en: He then had the two thousand horsemen who had come with him try together to turn the herd back; within less than three hundred paces the horses suddenly gave mournful cries, broke away, and bolted—the noise like a mountain falling.
units.literal: Thereupon he had the two thousand horsemen who had come with him together block the horses and turn them back; within less than three hundred paces they suddenly wailed, broke away, and fled—the sound like a collapsing mountain.

units.zh: 如是者十餘輩，一向一遠。
units.en: This happened more than ten times—each attempt sent them farther west.
units.literal: This happened more than ten times—they went one direction, then farther away.

units.zh: 樓力屈，又跪曰：「可寒，此非復人事。」
units.en: Lou's strength gave out; he knelt again and said, "Chukhan, this is no longer within human power."
units.literal: Lou's strength was exhausted; he knelt again and said: "Chukhan, this is no longer a matter within human power."

units.zh: 渾謂其部落曰：「我兄弟子孫，並應昌盛，廆當傳子及曾孫玄孫，其間可百餘年，我乃玄孫間始當顯耳。」
units.en: Hun told his tribesmen, "My brother's line and mine will both prosper; Hui's house will pass from son to great-grandson and beyond for perhaps a hundred years or more, while my line will not come to prominence until the generation of my great-great-grandsons."
units.literal: Hun said to his tribesmen: "My brother's descendants and mine should both flourish; Hui will pass the succession to sons, great-grandsons, and great-great-grandsons—between them perhaps a hundred-odd years—and only among my great-great-grandsons' generation will my line begin to rise."

units.zh: 於是遂西附陰山。
units.en: With that he went west and settled by the Yin Mountains.
units.literal: Thereupon he went west and attached himself to the Yin Mountains.

units.zh: 遭晉亂，遂得上隴。
units.en: When the Jin realm fell into chaos, he was able to reach the upper Long region.
units.literal: When the Jin fell into disorder, he was able to reach the upper Long region.

units.zh: 後廆追思渾，作阿干之歌。
units.en: Later, missing Hun, Hui composed the Song of Aghan.
units.literal: Later Hui, recalling Hun with longing, composed the Song of Aghan.

units.zh: 鮮卑呼兄為「阿干」。
units.en: The Xianbei call an elder brother "aghan."
units.literal: The Xianbei call an elder brother "aghan."

units.zh: 廆子孫竊號，以此歌為輦後大曲。
units.en: When Hui's descendants assumed royal titles, they made this song the great processional hymn played behind the imperial carriage.
units.literal: Hui's descendants usurped imperial titles and made this song the great piece behind the imperial carriage.

units.zh: 渾既上隴，出罕幵、西零。
units.en: Once Hun had reached the upper Long, his people spread into Hanqian and Xiling.
units.literal: After Hun had reached the upper Long, he came forth to Hanqian and Xiling.

units.zh: 西零，今之西平郡，罕幵，今枹罕縣。
units.en: Xiling is the present Xiping commandery; Hanqian is the present Fuhan county.
units.literal: Xiling is present-day Xiping commandery; Hanqian is present-day Fuhan county.

units.zh: 自枹罕以東千餘里，暨甘松，西至河南，南界昴城、龍涸。
units.en: From more than a thousand li east of Fuhan as far as Gansong, west to Henan, and south to the borders of Maocheng and Longgu.
units.literal: From more than a thousand li east of Fuhan as far as Gansong, west to Henan, south bounded by Maocheng and Longgu.

units.zh: 自洮水西南，極白蘭，數千里中，逐水草，廬帳居，以肉酪為糧。
units.en: From southwest of the Tao River to the limits of Bailan, over several thousand li they followed pasture and water, lived in felt tents, and lived on meat and curds.
units.literal: From southwest of the Tao River to the limits of Bailan, over several thousand li they followed grass and water, dwelt in felt tents, and took meat and curds as provisions.

units.zh: 西北諸雜種謂之為阿柴虜。
units.en: The various peoples of the northwest called them the A-Chai barbarians.
units.literal: The various tribes of the northwest called them the A-Chai barbarians.

units.zh: 渾年七十二死，有子六十人，長吐延嗣。
units.en: Hun died at seventy-two, leaving sixty sons; the eldest, Tuyan, succeeded him.
units.literal: Hun died at age seventy-two; he had sixty sons, and the eldest Tuyan succeeded him.

units.zh: 吐延身長七尺八寸，勇力過人，性刻暴，為昴城羌酋姜聰所刺，劍猶在體，呼子葉延，語其大將絕拔渥曰：[4]「吾氣絕，棺斂訖，便遠去保白蘭。
units.en: Tuyan stood seven feet eight inches tall, with courage and strength beyond ordinary men, but his nature was harsh and violent. The Qiang chieftain of Maocheng, Jiang Cong, stabbed him; the blade still stood in his body. He summoned his son Yeyan and told his great general Jueba Wo: [4] "When I am gone, once I am coffined, withdraw far away and secure Bailan.
units.literal: Tuyan was seven feet eight inches tall, his courage and strength surpassing other men; his nature was harsh and violent. He was stabbed by the Qiang chieftain of Maocheng, Jiang Cong; the sword still remained in his body. He called his son Yeyan and said to his great general Jueba Wo: [4] "When my breath ends, after the coffining is finished, go far away and hold Bailan.

units.zh: 白蘭地既嶮遠，又土俗懦弱，易為控御。
units.en: Bailan lies in rugged, remote country, and its peoples are weak by custom—easy to hold and govern.
units.literal: Bailan's territory is both rugged and remote, and its native customs are weak—easy to control.

units.zh: 葉延小，意乃欲授與餘人，恐倉卒終不能相制。
units.en: Yeyan is still young; I had considered passing rule to another, but I fear that in a sudden crisis he could not hold them in check.
units.literal: Yeyan is young; I had thought of entrusting rule to another, but I fear that in haste he would ultimately be unable to restrain them.

units.zh: 今以葉延付汝，汝竭股肱之力以輔之，孺子得立，吾無恨矣。」
units.en: I now entrust Yeyan to you—give all your strength to support him. If the boy can be established in power, I shall die without regret."
units.literal: Now I entrust Yeyan to you; exhaust the strength of your arms and legs to assist him—if the lad can be established, I have no regret."

units.zh: 抽劍而死。
units.en: He drew out the sword and died.
units.literal: He drew out the sword and died.

units.zh: 嗣位十三年，年三十五。
units.en: He reigned thirteen years and died at thirty-five.
units.literal: He succeeded to the position thirteen years and died at age thirty-five.

units.zh: 有子十二人。
units.en: He left twelve sons.
units.literal: He had twelve sons.

units.zh: 葉延少而勇果，年十歲，縛草為人，號曰姜聰，每旦輒射之，射中則喜，不中則號叫泣涕。
units.en: Yeyan was brave and resolute from boyhood. At ten he bound grass into a human figure, named it Jiang Cong, and shot at it every morning—when he hit it he rejoiced; when he missed he wailed and wept.
units.literal: Yeyan from youth was brave and resolute; at age ten he bound grass into a human figure, called it Jiang Cong, and every morning shot at it—if he hit it he rejoiced, if not he wailed and wept.

units.zh: 其母曰：「讎賊諸將已屠膾之，汝年小，何煩朝朝自苦如此。」
units.en: His mother said, "The enemy chieftain and his officers have already been butchered and minced for the pot—you are still young; why torment yourself morning after morning like this?"
units.literal: His mother said: "The enemy chieftain and his generals have already been butchered and minced—you are young; why trouble yourself morning after morning to torment yourself like this?"

units.zh: 葉延嗚咽不自勝，答母曰：「誠知無益，然葉延罔極之心，不勝其痛耳。」
units.en: Yeyan sobbed uncontrollably and answered, "I know it does no good, but my boundless grief for my father cannot bear the pain."
units.literal: Yeyan sobbed beyond control and answered his mother: "I truly know it is of no use, yet Yeyan's boundless heart cannot overcome the pain."

units.zh: 性至孝，母病，三日不能食，葉延亦不食。
units.en: He was profoundly filial: when his mother fell ill and could not eat for three days, Yeyan ate nothing either.
units.literal: His nature was supremely filial: when his mother fell ill and for three days could not eat, Yeyan also did not eat.

units.zh: 頗視書傳，自謂曾祖弈洛韓始封昌黎公，曰：「吾為公孫之子。
units.en: He read somewhat in books and records and held that his great-grandfather Yiluohan had first been enfeoffed as Duke of Changli, saying, "I am the grandson of a duke.
units.literal: He looked somewhat into books and records and said of himself that his great-grandfather Yiluohan had first been enfeoffed as Duke of Changli, saying: "I am a grandson of a duke.

units.zh: 案禮，公孫之子，得氏王父字。」
units.en: By ritual precedent, a duke's grandson may take his grandfather's style-name as his clan name."
units.literal: According to ritual, a grandson of a duke may take as surname the style-name of his grandfather."

units.zh: 命姓為吐谷渾氏。
units.en: He therefore took Tuyuhun as the clan name.
units.literal: He ordered that the clan surname be the Tuyuhun clan.

units.zh: 嗣立二十三年，年三十三。
units.en: He reigned twenty-three years and died at thirty-three.
units.literal: He succeeded and ruled twenty-three years, dying at age thirty-three.

units.zh: 有子四人。
units.en: He had four sons.
units.literal: He had four sons.

units.zh: 長子碎奚立。
units.en: His eldest son Suixi succeeded him.
units.literal: The eldest son Suixi succeeded.

units.zh: 碎奚性純謹，三弟專權，碎奚不能制，諸大將共誅之。
units.en: Suixi was pure and cautious in character, but his three younger brothers seized power and he could not restrain them; the great generals therefore executed the three brothers together.
units.literal: Suixi's nature was pure and cautious; his three younger brothers monopolized power and Suixi could not control them—the great generals together executed them.

units.zh: 碎奚憂哀不復攝事，遂立子視連為世子，委之事，號曰「莫賀郎」。
units.en: Grief-stricken, Suixi ceased to govern; he established his son Shilian as heir apparent, entrusted him with affairs, and styled him "Mohe Lang."
units.literal: Suixi, grief-stricken, no longer took up affairs of government; he thereupon established his son Shilian as heir apparent, entrusted affairs to him, and styled him "Mohe Lang."

units.zh: 「莫賀」，宋言父也。
units.en: "Mohe" means "father" in the language of Song.
units.literal: "Mohe" in Song language means father.

units.zh: 碎奚遂以憂死。
units.en: Suixi soon died of grief.
units.literal: Suixi thereupon died of grief.

units.zh: 在位二十五年，年四十二。
units.en: He had reigned twenty-five years and died at forty-two.
units.literal: He was on the throne twenty-five years and died at age forty-two.

units.zh: 有子六人。
units.en: He left six sons.
units.literal: He had six sons.

units.zh: 子視連以父憂卒，不遊娛，不酣宴。
units.en: His son Shilian, mourning a father who had died of grief, took no pleasure in sport and held no revels.
units.literal: His son Shilian, because his father died of grief, did not seek amusement or hold feasts of deep drinking.

units.zh: 在位十五年，年四十二。
units.en: He reigned fifteen years and died at forty-two.
units.literal: He was on the throne fifteen years and died at age forty-two.

units.zh: 有子二人，長曰視羆，次烏紇提。
units.en: He had two sons—the elder Shipi, the younger Wuheti.
units.literal: He had two sons: the elder was called Shipi, the younger Wuheti.

units.zh: [6]視羆嗣立十一年，年四十二。
units.en: [6] Shipi reigned eleven years and died at forty-two.
units.literal: [6] Shipi succeeded and ruled eleven years, dying at age forty-two.

units.zh: 子樹洛干等並小，弟烏紇提立。
units.en: His sons, including Shuluoqian, were still young, so his younger brother Wuheti succeeded.
units.literal: His sons Shuluoqian and the others were all young; his younger brother Wuheti succeeded.

units.zh: 紇提立八年，年三十五。
units.en: Wuheti reigned eight years and died at thirty-five.
units.literal: Hetie ruled eight years and died at age thirty-five.

units.zh: 視羆子樹洛干立，自稱車騎將軍，義熙初也。
units.en: Shipi's son Shuluoqian succeeded and styled himself General of the Agile Cavalry, at the beginning of the Yixi reign.
units.literal: Shipi's son Shuluoqian succeeded, styling himself General of the Agile Cavalry—it was the beginning of the Yixi era.

units.zh: 樹洛干死，弟阿犲自稱驃騎將軍。
units.en: When Shuluoqian died, his younger brother Achai styled himself General of the Valiant Cavalry.
units.literal: Shuluoqian died; his younger brother Achai styled himself General of the Valiant Cavalry.

units.zh: 譙縱亂蜀，阿犲遣其從子西彊公吐谷渾敕來泥拓土至龍涸、平康。
units.en: When Qiao Zong threw Shu into chaos, Achai sent his cousin, the Western Qiang Duke Tuyuhun Chilai Ni, to expand their territory as far as Longgu and Pingkang.
units.literal: When Qiao Zong threw Shu into disorder, Achai sent his cousin the Western Qiang Duke Tuyuhun Chilai Ni to expand territory as far as Longgu and Pingkang.

units.zh: 少帝景平中，阿犲遣使上表獻方物。
units.en: During the Jingping era of Emperor Shao, Achai sent envoys with a memorial offering local tribute.
units.literal: In the Jingping era of Emperor Shao, Achai sent envoys with a memorial presenting local products.

units.zh: 詔曰：「吐谷渾阿犲介在遐表，慕義可嘉，宜有寵任。
units.en: An edict declared, "Achai of the Tuyuhun, though he stands far beyond our borders, has shown admirable devotion to our cause and deserves favor and office.
units.literal: An edict said: "Tuyuhun's Achai stands far beyond the borders yet his admiration of righteousness is praiseworthy—he should receive favor and appointment.

units.zh: 今酬其來款，可督塞表諸軍事、安西將軍、沙州刺史、澆河公。」
units.en: In return for his embassy, let him be made Supervisor of Military Affairs beyond the Passes, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Jiaohe."
units.literal: Now in recompense for his coming with sincere regard, he may be Supervisor of Military Affairs beyond the Passes, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Jiaohe."

units.zh: 未及拜受，太祖元嘉三年，又詔加除命。
units.en: Before he could receive and accept these offices, in the third year of Emperor Taizu's Yuanjia reign a further edict added new appointments.
units.literal: Before he could receive investiture and accept office, in the third year of the Yuanjia era of Emperor Taizu there was again an edict adding further appointments.

units.zh: 未至而阿犲死，弟慕璝立。
units.en: The envoys had not yet arrived when Achai died; his younger brother Mugui succeeded.
units.literal: Before the envoys arrived Achai died; his younger brother Mugui succeeded.

units.zh: [7]六年，表曰：「大宋應運，四海宅心，臣亡兄阿犲慕義天朝，款情素著。
units.en: [7] In the sixth year he submitted a memorial: "Great Song has received Heaven's mandate and holds the hearts of all within the four seas. My late brother Achai long admired the celestial court, and his sincere devotion was well known.
units.literal: [7] In the sixth year he submitted a memorial saying: "Great Song has received the Mandate; within the four seas all hearts dwell here. My deceased elder brother Achai admired righteousness toward the celestial court; his sincere regard was always evident.

units.zh: 去年七月五日，謁者董湛至，宣傳明詔，顯授榮爵，而臣私門不幸，亡兄見背。
units.en: On the fifth day of the seventh month last year the attendant Dong Zhan arrived with your luminous edict, granting glorious ranks in full—but my house met private misfortune, and my brother was taken from us before he could receive them.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the seventh month last year the attendant Dong Zhan arrived, proclaiming the bright edict and clearly bestowing honored ranks, yet my private household met misfortune—my deceased brother was taken from us.

units.zh: 臣以懦弱，負荷後任，然天恩所報，本在臣門，若更反覆，懼停信命。
units.en: I am weak and unworthy, yet I now bear the succession; the grace Heaven meant to bestow was always meant for our house. If the grant is withdrawn and renewed, I fear your trust in us will falter.
units.literal: I, weak and timid, bear the later charge, yet the heavenly grace to be repaid was originally in my clan's gate—if there is further reversal, I fear the credence of the mandate will halt.

units.zh: 輒拜受寵任，奉遵上旨，伏願詳處，更授章策。」
units.en: I therefore bow to accept these honors and obey your command, humbly asking that you reconsider the matter and issue fresh seals and charters."
units.literal: I therefore bow and accept favor and appointment, obeying the superior intent; I prostrate myself hoping for detailed disposition and renewed bestowal of seals and charters."

units.zh: 七年，詔曰：「吐谷渾慕璝兄弟慕義，至誠可嘉，宜授策爵，以甄忠款。
units.en: In the seventh year an edict declared, "Mugui of the Tuyuhun and his brothers have shown admirable devotion and utmost sincerity; let charter and rank be granted to honor their loyalty.
units.literal: In the seventh year an edict said: "Tuyuhun's Mugui and his brothers admire righteousness; their utmost sincerity is praiseworthy—they should receive charter and rank to distinguish loyal regard.

units.zh: 可督塞表諸軍事、征西將軍、沙州刺史、隴西公。」
units.en: Let him be Supervisor of Military Affairs beyond the Passes, General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Longxi."
units.literal: He may be Supervisor of Military Affairs beyond the Passes, General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Longxi."

units.zh: 先是晉末，金城東允街縣胡人乞伏乾歸擁部眾據洮河、罕幵，自號隴西公。
units.en: Earlier, at the end of Jin, the Hu leader Qifu Gangui of Yunjie county east of Jincheng gathered his tribesmen, seized the Tao River region and Hanqian, and styled himself Duke of Longxi.
units.literal: Earlier, at the end of Jin, the Hu man Qifu Gangui of Yunjie county east of Jincheng gathered tribesmen, held the Tao River and Hanqian, and styled himself Duke of Longxi.

units.zh: 乾歸死，子熾磐立，遣使詣晉朝歸順，以為使持節、都督河西諸軍事、平西將軍，公如故。
units.en: When Gangui died, his son Chipan succeeded and sent envoys to the Jin court to submit; he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Hexi, and General Who Pacifies the West, retaining his ducal title.
units.literal: Gangui died; his son Chipan succeeded, sent envoys to the Jin court to submit, and was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Hexi, General Who Pacifies the West, duke as before.

units.zh: 高祖即位，進號安西大將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Chipan's title was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the West.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, his title was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the West.

units.zh: 熾磐死，子茂蔓立。
units.en: When Chipan died, his son Maoman succeeded.
units.literal: Chipan died; his son Maoman succeeded.

units.zh: [8]慕璝前後屢遣軍擊，茂蔓率部落東奔隴右，慕璝據有其地。
units.en: [8] Mugui repeatedly sent armies against him; Maoman led his tribes in flight east to the Long region, and Mugui seized his lands.
units.literal: [8] Mugui repeatedly sent armies to attack; Maoman led his tribes east fleeing to the right of Long, and Mugui seized his territory.

units.zh: 是歲，赫連定於長安為索虜拓跋燾所攻，擁秦戶口十餘萬西次罕幵，欲向涼州，慕璝距擊，大破之，生擒定。
units.en: That year Helian Ding at Chang'an was attacked by the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao; Ding gathered more than a hundred thousand Qin households and moved west to encamp at Hanqian, intending to march on Liangzhou. Mugui intercepted him, inflicted a crushing defeat, and took Ding alive.
units.literal: That year Helian Ding at Chang'an was attacked by the Northern Wei barbarian Tuoba Tao; he gathered more than a hundred thousand Qin households and moved west to encamp at Hanqian, intending to go toward Liangzhou. Mugui resisted and attacked, inflicting a great defeat and capturing Ding alive.

units.zh: 燾遣使求，慕璝以定與之。
units.en: Tao sent envoys to demand Ding; Mugui handed him over.
units.literal: Tao sent envoys to request him; Mugui gave Ding over to them.

units.zh: 九年，慕璝遣司馬趙敍奉貢獻，幷言二萬人捷。
units.en: In the ninth year Mugui sent Chief Clerk Zhao Xu with tribute and reported a victory over twenty thousand enemy troops.
units.literal: In the ninth year Mugui sent Chief Clerk Zhao Xu to present tribute and also reported a victory over twenty thousand men.

units.zh: 太祖加其使持節、散騎常侍、都督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、西秦河二州刺史、領護羌校尉，進爵隴西王。
units.en: Emperor Taizu further appointed him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Western Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Western Qin and He, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, and advanced him to King of Longxi.
units.literal: Emperor Taizu added for him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Governor of the two provinces of Western Qin and He, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, and advanced his rank to King of Longxi.

units.zh: 弟慕延為平東將軍，慕璝兄樹洛干子拾寅為平北將軍，阿豺子煒代鎮軍將軍。
units.en: His younger brother Muyan was made General Who Pacifies the East; Shiyin, son of Mugui's elder brother Shuluoqian, was made General Who Pacifies the North; and Wei, son of Achai, was made Acting General of the Garrison Army.
units.literal: His younger brother Muyan was made General Who Pacifies the East; Mugui's elder brother Shuluoqian's son Shiyin was made General Who Pacifies the North; Achai's son Wei was made Acting General of the Garrison Army.

units.zh: 詔慕璝南國將士，昔沒在佛佛者，並悉致。
units.en: An edict instructed Mugui to return all officers and soldiers of the southern states who had formerly been lost among the Fofo.
units.literal: An edict ordered Mugui: among the officers and soldiers of the southern states who in the past were lost among the Fofo, bring them all back.

units.zh: 慕璝遣送朱昕之等五十五戶，一百五十四人。
units.en: Mugui sent back Zhu Xinzhi and others—fifty-five households, one hundred fifty-four persons in all.
units.literal: Mugui sent back Zhu Xinzhi and others—fifty-five households, one hundred fifty-four persons.

units.zh: 慕璝死，弟慕延立，[9]遣使奉表。
units.en: When Mugui died, his younger brother Muyan succeeded [9] and sent envoys with a memorial.
units.literal: Mugui died; his younger brother Muyan succeeded [9] and sent envoys with a memorial.

units.zh: 十五年，除慕延使持節、散騎常侍、都督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、鎮西大將軍、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史、隴西王。
units.en: In the fifteenth year Muyan was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Western Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Guards the West, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, Governor of Western Qin and He, and King of Longxi.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year Muyan was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Guards the West, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, Governor of the two provinces of Western Qin and He, and King of Longxi.

units.zh: 十六年，改封河南王。
units.en: In the sixteenth year his title was changed to King of Henan.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year his enfeoffment was changed to King of Henan.

units.zh: 其年，以拾虔弟拾寅為平西將軍，慕延庶長子繁暱為撫軍將軍，慕延嫡子瑍為左將軍、河南王世子。
units.en: That same year Shiyin, younger brother of Shiqian, was made General Who Pacifies the West; Muyan's eldest son by a concubine, Fan'ai, was made General Who Pacifies the Army; and Muyan's legitimate son Min was made Left General and Heir Apparent of the King of Henan.
units.literal: That year Shiqian's younger brother Shiyin was made General Who Pacifies the West; Muyan's eldest son by a concubine Fan'ai was made General Who Pacifies the Army; Muyan's legitimate son Min was made Left General and Heir Apparent of the King of Henan.

units.zh: 十九年，追贈阿豺本號安西、秦沙三州諸軍事、沙州刺史、領護羌校尉、隴西王。
units.en: In the nineteenth year Achai was posthumously granted his former titles—General Who Pacifies the West, Commander of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Qin and Sha, Governor of Shazhou, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, and King of Longxi.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year Achai was posthumously granted his former titles: Commander of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Qin and Sha, Governor of Shazhou, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, and King of Longxi.

units.zh: 索虜拓跋燾遣軍擊慕延，大破之，慕延率部落西奔白蘭，攻破于闐國。
units.en: The Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao sent an army against Muyan and inflicted a crushing defeat; Muyan led his tribes west in flight to Bailan and overran the kingdom of Khotan.
units.literal: The Northern Wei barbarian Tuoba Tao sent an army to attack Muyan and inflicted a great defeat; Muyan led his tribes in flight west to Bailan and broke the state of Khotan.

units.zh: 慮虜復至，二十七年，遣使上表云：「若不自固者，欲率部曲入龍涸越嶲門。」
units.en: Fearing another attack from the barbarians, in the twenty-seventh year he sent envoys with a memorial: "If I cannot hold my ground, I wish to lead my followers through Longgu and over the Yuexi Gate into your territory."
units.literal: Fearing the barbarians would come again, in the twenty-seventh year he sent envoys with a memorial saying: "If I cannot hold my own, I wish to lead my followers through Longgu and over the Yuexi Gate."

units.zh: 并求牽車，獻烏丸帽、女國金酒器、胡王金釧等物。
units.en: He also requested an imperial carriage and presented a Wuhuan cap, golden wine vessels from the Land of Women, a golden bracelet of the Hu kings, and other gifts.
units.literal: He also requested an imperial carriage and presented a Wuhuan cap, golden wine vessels from the Land of Women, a golden bracelet of the Hu kings, and other objects.

units.zh: 太祖賜以牽車，若虜至不自立，聽入越嶲。
units.en: Emperor Taizu granted him a carriage and permission to enter through Yuexi if the barbarians came and he could not hold his ground.
units.literal: Emperor Taizu granted him an imperial carriage; if the barbarians came and he could not stand firm, he was permitted to enter through Yuexi.

units.zh: 虜竟不至也。
units.en: In the end the barbarians did not come.
units.literal: The barbarians in the end did not come.

units.zh: 慕延死，拾寅自立。
units.en: When Muyan died, Shiyin took power on his own authority.
units.literal: Muyan died; Shiyin established himself on his own.

units.zh: 二十九年，以拾寅為使持節、督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、安西將軍、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史、河南王。
units.en: In the twenty-ninth year Shiyin was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, Governor of Western Qin and He, and King of Henan.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Shiyin was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, Governor of the two provinces of Western Qin and He, and King of Henan.

units.zh: 拾寅東破索虜，加開府儀同三司。
units.en: When Shiyin defeated the Northern Wei forces in the east, he was further granted the title of Director with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: Shiyin defeated the Northern Wei barbarians in the east and was given the additional title of Director with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.

units.zh: 世祖大明五年，拾寅遣使獻善舞馬，四角羊。
units.en: In the fifth year of Emperor Shizu's Daming reign, Shiyin sent envoys presenting fine dancing horses and four-horned sheep.
units.literal: In the fifth year of the Daming era of Emperor Shizu, Shiyin sent envoys presenting dancing horses of fine quality and four-horned sheep.

units.zh: 皇太子、王公以下上舞馬歌者二十七首。
units.en: The crown prince, princes, dukes, and officials below them submitted twenty-seven songs in praise of the dancing horses.
units.literal: The crown prince, kings, dukes, and those below submitted twenty-seven songs on the dancing horses.

units.zh: 太宗泰始三年，進號征西大將軍。
units.en: In the third year of Emperor Taizong's Taishi reign, Shiyin's title was advanced to Grand General Who Conquers the West.
units.literal: In the third year of the Taishi era of Emperor Taizong, his title was advanced to Grand General Who Conquers the West.

units.zh: 五年，拾寅奉表獻方物，以弟拾皮為平西將軍、金城公。
units.en: In the fifth year Shiyin sent a memorial with local tribute and appointed his younger brother Shipi General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Jincheng.
units.literal: In the fifth year Shiyin submitted a memorial presenting local products and made his younger brother Shipi General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Jincheng.

units.zh: 前廢帝又進號車騎大將軍。
units.en: The Deposed Former Emperor further advanced his title to Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor of the Former Reign again advanced his title to Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.

units.zh: 其國西有黃沙，南北一百二十里，東西七十里，不生草木，沙州因此為號。
units.en: West of their territory lies a tract of yellow sand one hundred twenty li from north to south and seventy li from east to west, where nothing grows; the province of Shazhou takes its name from this desert.
units.literal: West of their state is yellow sand, one hundred twenty li north to south and seventy li east to west, where grass and trees do not grow; Shazhou takes its name from this.

units.zh: 屈真川有鹽池，甘谷嶺北有雀鼠同穴，或在山嶺，或在平地，雀色白，鼠色黃，地生黃紫花草，便有雀鼠穴。
units.en: The Quzhen River has salt ponds. North of Gangu Ridge are the famed "sparrow-and-rat shared burrows," found on ridges or on flat ground: the sparrows are white, the rats yellow, and wherever yellow and purple wildflowers grow, sparrow-and-rat burrows appear.
units.literal: Quzhen River has salt ponds; north of Gangu Ridge there are sparrow-and-rat shared burrows, sometimes on mountain ridges, sometimes on level ground—the sparrows are white, the rats yellow; where the ground produces yellow and purple flowers and grass, there are sparrow-and-rat burrows.

units.zh: 白蘭土出黃金、銅、鐵。
units.en: The soil of Bailan yields gold, copper, and iron.
units.literal: Bailan's soil produces gold, copper, and iron.

units.zh: 其國雖隨水草，大抵治慕賀川。
units.en: Though their people moved with pasture and water, their government was centered broadly at Muhe River.
units.literal: Although their state follows grass and water, broadly they govern at Muhe River.

units.en: [10] (Editorial note.)
units.literal: [10] (Editorial note.)

units.zh: 史臣曰：吐谷渾逐草依泉，擅強塞表，毛衣肉食，取資佃畜，而錦組繒紈，見珍殊俗，徒以商譯往來，故禮同北面。
units.en: The historiographer writes: The Tuyuhun followed pasture and spring water and held sway beyond the frontier passes, living on meat and hides and the herds they tended; yet their brocades and silks were prized in distant lands. Only because merchants and interpreters shuttled back and forth were they received with the ceremony due those who face the throne.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Tuyuhun followed grass and clung to springs, holding power beyond the passes; they wore fur and ate meat, drawing sustenance from herded livestock, yet brocades, silks, and fine gauze were prized in alien lands—only because merchants and interpreters came and went were they treated with ceremony like those who face north.

units.zh: 自昔哲王，雖存柔遠，要荒回隔，禮文弗被，大不過子，義著春秋。
units.en: Wise kings of old, though gentle toward distant peoples, still kept the outer and wild realms at arm's length—ritual and civilization did not reach them, and titles never rose above that of a feudal son, as the Spring and Autumn Annals make plain.
units.literal: From antiquity wise kings, though they preserved gentleness toward the distant, kept the outer and wild regions separated by circuitous distance—ritual and culture did not reach them; enfeoffment did not exceed the rank of son, as the meaning is set forth in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

units.zh: 晉、宋垂典，不修古則，遂爵班上等，秩擬台光。
units.en: Jin and Song established precedent without restoring ancient norms, granting the highest noble ranks and offices that rivaled the brilliance of the central court.
units.literal: Jin and Song handed down their statutes without restoring ancient rules, and so enfeoffment ranks reached the highest grades and offices were made to match the brilliance of the terrace.

units.zh: 辮髮稱賀，非尚簪冕，言語不通，寧敷袞職。
units.en: They came with braided hair to offer congratulations, not to honor caps and coronets; their languages were not mutually intelligible—how could they bear the duties of court office?
units.literal: With braided hair they offered congratulations—they did not esteem caps and coronets; their speech was not mutually intelligible—how could they bear the duties of court robes?

units.zh: 雖復苞篚歲臻，事惟賈道，金罽氈毦，非用斯急，送迓煩擾，獲不如亡。
units.en: Though tribute arrived every year, the exchange was merely trade: gold brocade, felt rugs, and woolens were not urgently needed at court, and the trouble of sending envoys to receive them cost more than it was worth.
units.literal: Though tribute bundles arrived year by year, the affair was only the merchant's way—gold brocade, felt rugs, and wool pile were not urgently needed; sending and receiving was troublesome and vexing—the gain was not equal to the loss.

units.zh: 若令肅慎年朝，越裳歲饗，固不容以異見書，取高前策。
units.en: If the Sushen came to court every year and the Yuechang offered tribute annually, one could hardly record them as foreign subjects and call that an improvement on earlier policy.
units.literal: If one were to have the Sushen come to court yearly and the Yuechang feast yearly, one certainly could not record them as aliens and take this as elevating the earlier policy.

units.zh: 聖人謂之荒服，此言蓋有以也。
units.en: The sages spoke of the "wild service" for such lands—and this judgment surely has its reasons.
units.literal: The sages called such lands the wild service—this remark surely has its grounds.

units.zh: 鮮卑越質詰歸率戶二萬叛乞伏乾歸，降於興，興處之于成紀，拜使持節、鎮西將軍、平襄公。
units.en: Yuezhi Jiegui brought twenty thousand households from Qifu Gangui to Yao Xing, who settled them at Chengji and titled him general who guards the west, duke of Pingxiang.
units.literal: The Xianbei Yuezhi Jiegui led twenty thousand households in revolt from Qifu Gangui and surrendered to Xing; Xing settled them at Chengji and appointed him Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Pingxiang.

units.zh: 使碩德率隴右諸軍伐乞伏乾歸，興潛軍赴之，乾歸敗走，降其部眾三萬六千，收鎧馬六萬匹。
units.en: Yao Shuode struck Qifu Gangui while Yao Xing reinforced him, taking thirty-six thousand prisoners and sixty thousand horses.
units.literal: He ordered Shuode to lead the various armies of Longyou to campaign against Qifu Gangui; Xing secretly marched to join him; Gangui was defeated and fled; he surrendered thirty-six thousand of his following and collected sixty thousand suits of armor and horses.

units.zh: 興遣齊難及鎮西姚詰、鎮遠乞伏乾歸、鎮遠趙曜等步騎四萬，迎隆於河西。
units.en: Xing sent Qi Nan with Yao Jie, Qifu Gangui, Zhao Yao, and others, forty thousand foot and horse, to welcome Lü Long west of the river.
units.literal: Xing sent Qi Nan together with General Who Guards the West Yao Jie, General Who Guards the Distance Qifu Gangui, General Who Guards the Distance Zhao Yao, and others, forty thousand foot and horse, to welcome Long west of the river.

units.zh: 時劉裕誅桓玄，迎復安帝，玄衛將軍、新安王桓謙，臨原王桓怡，雍州刺史桓蔚，左衛將軍桓謐，中書令桓胤，將軍何澹之等奔於興。
units.en: After Liu Yu killed Huan Xuan and restored Emperor An, Huan Qian, Huan Yi, Huan Wei, Huan Mi, Huan Yin, He Danzhi, and others fled to Yao Xing.
units.literal: At the time Liu Yu had executed Huan Xuan, welcomed and restored Emperor An; Xuan's Guard General and Prince of Xin'an Huan Qian, Prince of Linyuan Huan Yi, Inspector of Yongzhou Huan Wei, General of the Left Guard Huan Mi, Director of the Secretariat Huan Yin, General He Danzhi, and others fled to Xing.

units.zh: 劉裕遣大參軍衡凱之詣姚顯，請通和，顯遣吉默報之，自是聘使不絕。
units.en: Liu Yu sent his senior staff officer Heng Kaizhi to Yao Xian to request peace; Yao Xian sent Ji Mo in reply, and from then on embassies were unceasing.
units.literal: Liu Yu sent senior staff officer Heng Kaizhi to Yao Xian begging open peace; Xian sent Ji Mo to answer him; from this envoys on friendly missions were unceasing.

units.zh: 群臣咸諫以為不可，興曰：「天下之善一也，劉裕拔萃起微，匡輔晉室，吾何惜數郡而不成其美乎！」
units.en: Ministers objected; Yao Xing said, "The good under heaven is one; Liu Yu, outstanding from humble beginnings, aids and supports the Jin house—why should I begrudge several commanderies and not complete his beauty!"
units.literal: The host of ministers all remonstrated that it could not be done; Xing said: "The good under heaven is one; Liu Yu, outstanding from humble beginnings, aids and supports the Jin house—why should I begrudge several commanderies and not complete his beauty!"

units.zh: 乙亥，立桂陽公義真為廬陵王，彭城公義隆為宜都王，第四皇子義康為彭城王。
units.en: On the day yihai, the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen, was established as Prince of Luling; the Duke of Pengcheng, Yilong, as Prince of Yidu; the fourth prince, Yikang, as Prince of Pengcheng.
units.literal: On the day yihai, the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen, was established as Prince of Luling; the Duke of Pengcheng, Yilong, as Prince of Yidu; the fourth prince, Yikang, as Prince of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 八月戊午，西中郎將、荊州刺史宜都王義隆進號鎮西將軍。
units.en: In the eighth month, on the day wuwu, General of the Western Interior, Governor of Jing Province, Prince of Yidu Yilong was advanced to General Who Stabilizes the West.
units.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wuwu, the General of the Western Interior, Governor of Jing Province, Prince of Yidu Yilong was advanced to General Who Stabilizes the West.

units.zh: 五月丙午，進河南王吐谷渾拾寅號驃騎大將軍。
units.en: Fifth month, day bingwu: Murong Shibin of Henan was promoted to general-in-chief who spreads might.
units.literal: Fifth month, day bingwu: Prince Murong Shibin of Henan was advanced to General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might.

units.zh: 乙卯，河南王吐谷渾拾寅奉表貢獻。
units.en: Day yimao: Murong Shibin of Henan sent tribute with a memorial.
units.literal: On day yimao Prince Murong Shibin of Henan presented a memorial with tribute.

units.zh: 冬十月戊子，以河南王世子吐谷渾易度侯爲西秦、河二州刺史，河南王。
units.en: Winter, tenth month, day wuzi: Yidu Hou of the Tuyuhun, heir of the king of Henan, was made inspector of West Qin and He and confirmed as king of Henan.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter, day wuzi, the heir of the King of Henan, Tuyuhun Yidu Hou, was made Inspector of West Qin and He, and King of Henan.

units.zh: 是歲，魏主拓跋嗣薨，子燾立。
units.en: That year, the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died and his son Tao succeeded him.
units.literal: That year, the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died and his son Tao succeeded.

units.zh: 立其妻梁氏為王后，子璝為太子，封子延陽平公，昌太原公，倫酒泉公，定平原公，滿河南公，安中山公。
units.en: He made his wife Lady Liang queen, his son Gui crown prince, and enfeoffed Yan as Duke of Yangping, Chang as Duke of Taiyuan, Lun as Duke of Jiuquan, Ding as Duke of Pingyuan, Man as Duke of Henan, and An as Duke of Zhongshan.
units.literal: He installed his wife Lady Liang as queen, his son Gui as crown prince, enfeoffed his son Yan as Duke of Yangping, Chang as Duke of Taiyuan, Lun as Duke of Jiuquan, Ding as Duke of Pingyuan, Man as Duke of Henan, and An as Duke of Zhongshan.

units.zh: 帝王者，系天為子，是為徽赫實與天連，今改姓曰赫連氏，庶協皇天之意，永享無疆大慶。
units.en: The emperor is heaven's son, joined to the sky; I change my surname to Helian to accord with heaven and enjoy endless blessing.
units.literal: The emperor-king is tied to Heaven as son; this is splendor and greatness truly joined with Heaven; now I change my surname to Helian, hoping to accord with Heaven's intent and eternally enjoy boundless great celebration.

units.zh: 沮渠蒙遜、吐谷渾阿犲並遣使朝貢。
units.en: Juqu Mengxun and Tuguhun A'ai both sent envoys to court with tribute.
units.literal: Juqu Mengxun and Tuguhun A'ai both sent envoys with tribute.

units.zh: 以阿犲為安西將軍、沙州刺史，封澆河公。
units.en: A'ai was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Shazhou, and created Duke of Jiaohe.
units.literal: A'ai was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Shazhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiaohe.

units.zh: 廢帝即位，為寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, Que was made Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou with overall military authority.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Que was made Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou with overall command.

units.zh: 少帝既誅顏師伯、柳元景等，狂悖益甚，以領軍徵玄謨。
units.en: After the Deposed Emperor killed Yan Shibo, Liu Yuanying, and the rest, his madness deepened. He recalled Xuanmo as General of the Palace Guard.
units.literal: After the Deposed Emperor had executed Yan Shibo, Liu Yuanying, and others, his frenzy grew worse. He summoned Xuanmo as General of the Palace Guard.

units.zh: 少帝大怒。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor flew into a rage.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor was greatly enraged.

units.zh: 當少帝失道，多所殺戮，而能冒履不測，傾心輔弼，斯可謂忘身徇國者歟。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor abandoned the Way and slaughtered without measure, Xuanmo still risked the unknown and gave his heart to steady the throne—can this be anything but forgetting self for the sake of the realm?
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor lost the Way and killed many, Xuanmo could still brave the unknown and give his heart to aid the throne—may this not be called forgetting self and serving the state?

units.zh: 少帝追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
units.en: Emperor Shao posthumously honored him as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
units.literal: Emperor Shao posthumously awarded him Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and added the title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

units.zh: 永初三年，致仕，拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
units.en: In the third year of Yongchu he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple cord.
units.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he retired from office, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and granted the golden seal and purple cord.

units.zh: 後四年，譙縱據蜀稱成都王。
units.en: Four years later Qiao Zong carved out Chengdu in Shu.
units.literal: Four years later Qiao Zong held Shu as Prince of Chengdu.

units.zh: 鮮卑慕容廆庶兄吐谷渾爲氐王。
units.en: Tuyuhun, an elder half-brother of the Xianbei Murong Hui by a concubine, became king of the Di.
units.literal: Tuyuhun, Murong Hui of the Xianbei's elder brother by a concubine, became king of the Di.

units.zh: 在益州西北，亘數千里。
units.en: They lay northwest of Yizhou and stretched for thousands of li.
units.literal: They were northwest of Yizhou, stretching several thousand li.

units.zh: 曄轉醉，子藹亦醉，取地土及果皮以擲曄，呼曄為別駕數十聲。
units.en: Ye grew still more drunk. His son Fan Ai, also drunk, picked up dirt and fruit peels and threw them at Ye, calling him "Assistant Administrator" dozens of times.
units.literal: Ye grew increasingly drunk; his son Fan Ai, also drunk, took earth and fruit peels to throw at Ye, calling Ye "Assistant Administrator" dozens of times.

units.zh: 曄及子藹、遙、叔蔞、孔熙先及弟休先、景先、思先、熙先子桂甫、桂甫子白民、謝綜及弟約、仲承祖、許耀，諸所連及，並伏誅。
units.en: Fan Ye and his sons Fan Ai, Fan Yao, and Fan Shulou; Kong Xixian and his younger brothers Kong Xiuxian, Kong Jingxian, and Kong Sixian; Xixian's son Kong Guifu and Guifu's son Kong Baimin; Xie Zong and his younger brother Xie Yue; Zhong Chengzu; and Xu Yao—all those implicated were put to death.
units.literal: Fan Ye and his sons Fan Ai, Fan Yao, and Fan Shulou; Kong Xixian and his younger brothers Kong Xiuxian, Kong Jingxian, and Kong Sixian; Xixian's son Kong Guifu and Guifu's son Kong Baimin; Xie Zong and his younger brother Xie Yue; Zhong Chengzu; and Xu Yao—all those implicated were executed.

units.zh: 死時年二十。
units.en: Fan Ai was twenty when he died.
units.literal: At death Fan Ai was twenty.

units.zh: 藹幼而整潔，衣服竟歲未嘗有塵點。
units.en: Fan Ai was neat and orderly from childhood; his clothes went a whole year without a speck of dust.
units.literal: Fan Ai from youth was neat and clean; his clothes throughout the year never once had a speck of dust.

units.zh: 藹子魯連，吳興昭公主外孫，請全生命，亦得遠徙，世祖即位得還。
units.en: Fan Ai's son Lulian, a grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded for his life and was likewise exiled to a distant place; when Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, he was permitted to return.
units.literal: Fan Ai's son Lulian, grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded to spare his life; he too was exiled afar; when Shizu ascended the throne he was allowed to return.

units.zh: 藹曰：「今日何緣復恚？
units.en: Fan Ai said: "What reason is there to be angry today?
units.literal: Fan Ai said: "What cause today to be angry again?

units.zh: 凝，太宗世禦史中丞，出為晉陵太守。
units.en: Ning was director of the censorate under the Taizong Emperor and went out as administrator of Jinling.
units.literal: Ning was Director of the Censorate under the Taizong Emperor and went out as Administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 太宗初與四方同反，兵敗歸降，以補劉湛冠軍府主簿。
units.en: In Taizong's first year he rebelled with the four quarters; defeated, he surrendered and was made chief clerk in Liu Zhan's champion army.
units.literal: In the first year of the Taizong Emperor he rebelled with the four quarters; when his army was defeated he returned and surrendered, and was appointed chief clerk in Liu Zhan's army of the champion general.
